newsitem.title: UK: Growth, jobs to be in focus ahead of EMU - Fleming.
newsitem.headline: Growth, jobs to be in focus ahead of EMU - Fleming.

text.p: An emphasis on growth and employment will feature prominently in the run-up to European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), investment bank Robert Fleming & Co. said in a report on Monday.

Flemings gave five potential scenarios for EMU and said all shared two possibilities -- "some form of single currency area led by Germany and a renewed emphasis on growth and employment, particularly in Britain and France".

The five scenarios range from the German Constitutional Court blocking a wider EMU that includes Italy and Spain to currency turmoil among non-EMU European currencies leading to a modified EMU run by the Bundesbank.
In just one of the five potential outcomes does a broad-based EMU result, only after Germany delays a decision on joining until after the country's general election in 1998.

A single currency emerges in all five cases, but in four out of the five only after significant upheaval and disagreement within the European Union. The build-up to EMU over the last five years was marked by a deteriorating fiscal situation and anemic growth in Europe, Flemings said.
The report was timed to coincide with the fifth anniversary of the Maastricht Treaty on Monday, Flemings said.
